Current verdict

  • The structural C1–Rm–C2 split fixes the gross inlet integral: LAD D/T rises from the rejected V1 value 0.526 to about 0.85 while systolic flow remains finite.
  • The terminal accepted iteration meets the declared shadow closure gates: max log-tone change ≤ 1e-4 and max relative volume drift ≤ 1e-5. This is not closed-loop P1.
  • Matching mean ENDO flow requires LAD ENDO R1 scale 0.118 versus the maximal-dilation floor 0.089. A healthy rest state that consumes nearly all reserve is not acceptable.
  • Peak ratio is protocol-sensitive: 1.11 using MVC→AoVC but 4.63 using AoVO→AoVC. Neither is a hard gate until the cited measurement protocol and site are aligned.
  • The inlet peak is 0.146 s after AoVC; ENDO Q1 and Qm must not be judged as the same measurement site.
  • LAD ENDO Qm peaks 0.574 s after AoVC and only 0.072 of its diastolic forward volume occurs in the first 200 ms. The tissue-transfer phase remains too late for a healthy release.
  • CV→RA has no reverse flow, but LAD ENDO Q2 backfills from CV for 0.26 s in diastole. A clean outlet trace does not establish normal internal venous physiology.
  • Therefore this is a mechanism diagnostic, not a healthy canonical coronary release.

What is deliberately absent

  • No hard diode, no valve-like gating, no inertance, no prescribed flow waveform.
  • No oxygen state; “metabolic” tone is only a reduced accepted flow-demand controller.
  • No source feedback and no fixed-TBV atomic coupling yet; Ao, RA and IMP are replayed from the same terminal main-wire beat.
  • The 2×2 ablation rejects a one-knob compliance or resistance-partition repair. Next: construct the normal reference resistance under the beating boundary, then audit IMP and collapse ownership before adding conduit wave impedance.
